purpose: Source-referenced one-electron ion spectral rows for a hydrogen-like ion benchmark gate.

mass_convention.description: Use reduced-mass R_Z = R_infinity * Z^2 / (1 + m_e / M_nucleus).

lithium_7_relative_atomic_mass_u.source: NIST Atomic Weights and Isotopic Compositions for Lithium

carbon_12_relative_atomic_mass_u.source: CODATA/NIST exact carbon-12 atomic mass definition

mass_convention.lithium_7_nucleus_mass_approximation: Li-7 atomic mass minus three electron masses; electron binding energy mass correction is neglected at the current ppm-scale gate.
mass_convention.carbon_12_nucleus_mass_approximation: C-12 atomic mass minus six electron masses; electron binding energy mass correction is neglected at the current ppm-scale gate.

lines.name: He II Lyman-alpha strong-line component
lines.source: NIST Handbook of Basic Atomic Spectroscopic Data, Strong Lines of Helium
lines.source_locator: Strong Lines of Helium table; He II wavelength 303.7804 A
lines.line_structure_note: NIST strong-line table lists nearby He II components at 303.7804 A and 303.7858 A; the current verifier treats this row as a representative fine-structure component, not a QED/fine-structure validation.

lines.name: Li III Lyman-alpha blend
lines.source: Li et al., Plasma Science and Technology 23 (2021) 075102, table of lithium lines citing NIST
lines.source_locator: Table 3; Li III 2p -> 1s; this work 135.02 +/- 0.03 A; NIST 135.0 A
lines.line_structure_note: Table groups 2p 2P fine-structure components into a single observed/NIST wavelength; this is not a fine-structure validation.

lines.name: C VI Lyman-alpha reference wavelength
lines.source: NIST Reference Wavelengths from Atomic Spectra
lines.source_locator: Reference wavelengths table; C VI wavelength 33.7360 A, wavenumber 2964195 cm^-1
lines.line_structure_note: Reference row is treated as a representative C VI Lyman-alpha target; this is not a fine-structure/QED validation.

claim_boundary: These rows may support a first hydrogen-like ion benchmark gate only. They do not validate neutral helium, many-electron atoms, QED corrections, or UET first-principles atomic theory.
